_comment: The bucket policy for the sample's bucket. scripts/setup.sh drops this _comment key
(S3 rejects an unknown top-level key), fills in the placeholders and calls
s3:PutBucketPolicy with the result:
<POD_ROLE_ARN>        the pod's dedicated EKS Pod Identity role, which carries no
identity policies of its own, so every permission it has on
this bucket is written here
<S3_BUCKET>           the bucket name, from .env
<S3_CIPHERTEXT_KEY>   the encrypted file
<S3_MANIFEST_KEY>     the manifest holding the wrapped data key and the nonce
The one allow is two object reads, named key by key: no s3:ListBucket, no write, no
delete, and no prefix wildcard. The pod reads the manifest to find the wrapped data
key, and the ciphertext to decrypt. Nothing here grants any KMS action: releasing the
data key is the key policy's decision, and it is conditional on attestation.
This is the whole of the role's access to the bucket. S3 lets a bucket policy grant a
principal in the same account on its own, so the role needs no identity policy, and
the sample gives it none.
The second statement refuses any request that is not over TLS, for every principal.
Sources, both public: bucket policies in the Amazon S3 User Guide,
'Using bucket policies'; aws:SecureTransport in the IAM User Guide's global condition
keys.
